title: 4 Best Blenders for Smoothies, Soups and Frozen Drinks
metaDescription: The best blenders by type: high-performance, value high-performance, full-size budget and personal, with honest limitations.
lede: A blender that suits you depends on what you blend and how often. These four cover daily smoothie drinkers to people who want one machine for soups, nut butters and frozen drinks, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.

products.name: Vitamix 5200 Blender
products.bestFor: daily heavy use, nut butters and hot soups
products.blurb: A long-running high-performance blender with a tall 64-ounce container and a variable speed dial. Friction from the blades can heat soup in the container.
strengths: Very smooth results with fibrous greens and nuts
limitations: Tall container may not fit under some cabinets
Expensive compared with full-size budget blenders
Tall jar is less suited to very small batches

products.name: Vitamix E310 Explorian Blender
products.bestFor: people who want Vitamix performance for less
products.blurb: A lower-priced Vitamix with a shorter 48-ounce container, ten speeds and a pulse switch. It suits smaller households.
strengths: Shorter jar fits under most cabinets
limitations: Shorter warranty than premium Vitamix models

products.name: Ninja Professional BL610 Blender
products.bestFor: frozen drinks and big batches on a budget
products.blurb: A 1,000-watt blender with a large 72-ounce pitcher and stacked blades that crush ice quickly.
limitations: Not as smooth as high-performance blenders with greens and seeds
Removable blade assembly is sharp and needs care when cleaning

products.name: NutriBullet Pro 900 Personal Blender
products.blurb: A compact 900-watt personal blender. You blend straight into the cup, then swap the blade for a to-go lid.
strengths: Blend and drink from the same cup
limitations: Only makes one or two servings at a time

howWeChose: We chose one blender per type so you can pick by use rather than by wattage.
Picks are based on manufacturer specs, warranties, independent reviews and owner reports.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.

faqs.q: Is a high-performance blender worth it?
faqs.a: If you blend daily, make nut butters or want very smooth green smoothies, many owners say yes. For occasional frozen drinks, a full-size budget blender is usually enough.
Only in blenders the manufacturer says are suitable, such as full-size Vitamix models. Personal blenders with sealed cups should not be used with hot liquids because pressure can build up.
